identity.name: Hellenic League of the Lamian War

land.text: the Greek states that 'revolted after Alexander's death': Athens, the Aetolians, Thessaly, Phocis, Locris and the Peloponnesian allies

predecessors.note: The members were allies of the League of Corinth under Macedonian hegemony (vassal tint of the macedonian-empire dossier 337-323); the coalition is their revolt.

land.text: Thessaly recovered after Crannon (6 August 322), Athens garrisoned at Munychia (18 September 322) and stripped of 'possessions outside Attica' (Oropus, Samos)

successors.note: Macedonian hegemony restored: the macedonian-empire dossier resumes the Greek vassal tint from September 322.

land.text: Aetolia, which 'was the only state to continue the war' and was never reduced (Antipater and Craterus's Aetolian campaign of 322/321 was abandoned)

successors.note: The Aetolian League keeps its own colour throughout; see its dossier.

capitals.name: Athens
capitals.note: Athens led the alliance (Leosthenes, then Antiphilus, commanded); the coalition had no federal seat.

union.text: Phocis, Locris, Doris, Malis (except Lamia), Oetaea, Ainis, Phthiotic Achaea
Aetolia and Elis (Achaea is not on the list)
Athamania, Dolopia and the Molossian faction (western uplands)

correction.text: the members the Lamian War page lists: Athens, the Aetolian League, Thessaly (except Pelinna), Oetaea, Achaea Phthiotis, Malis (except Lamia), Doris, Locris, Phocis, Ainis, Dolopia, Athamania, Leucas, 'some Molossians'; in the Peloponnese Argos, Sicyon, Epidaurus, Troezen, Phlius, Elis, Messenia; Carystus; Rhodes possibly

keyframe_review.note: 23 k km2 for 323-319: Attica, Thessaly and Aetolia only, and four years too long. The war ran from 'probably in the beginning of September' 323 to Crannon on '6 August 322' and the surrender of Athens ('Munychia... taken on 18 September 322'); the shape should end in 322. Membership was wider (Peloponnesian members above) and did not include Boeotia, Euboea (except Carystus), Corinth, Sparta ('Sparta refused to join') or Megalopolis. Confidence 2: tribal members are approximated by radii. Drawn hatched over the Macedonian vassal tint (rule 5), or, for the Aetolians, over their own colour.

region.text: Athens, the Aetolians and the first allies

ledger.note: September 323: 'Athens was already preparing for war when the news of Alexander's death in June 323 BC became known'; 'war started shortly after, probably in the beginning of September'; the Aetolian 'alliance was possibly concluded in mid-September 323 BC'. The Thessalians went over to the Greeks at the outset, and Antipater 'remained besieged in Lamia for most of the winter 323-322 BC'.

region.text: Thessaly and the Spercheios valley (Lamia), the war zone

ledger.note: September 323 to August 322: rule 6 blend over the fighting zone. The macedonian-empire dossier carries the matching pair.

region.text: Phocis and the other states of central Greece west of Boeotia

ledger.note: 27 October 323: 'the treaty between Athens and Phokis is dated from 27 October'. Locris, Doris, Malis, Oetaea, Ainis joined in the same months (undated on the page). Boeotia and Euboea stayed Macedonian.

region.text: Sicyon, Argos and the Acte, Elis and Messenia

ledger.note: 23 December 323: 'Sicyon's treaty with Athens is dated 23 December'. Argos, Epidaurus, Troezen, Phlius, Elis and Messenia are listed as Peloponnesian members without dates; 'Sparta refused to join'.
6 August 322: 'The final battle took place at Crannon on 6 August 322 BC' (Heckel gives 5 August), a Macedonian victory; the Greek cities then made separate terms.

August 322: after Crannon Antipater took the Thessalian and central Greek cities one by one as they 'made separate terms'. [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: counterpart macedonian-empire to greek-city-states: the members return to the Greek city-states row (its /ledger/47, September 322), which Macedon then takes as vassals (macedonian-empire /ledger/30).]

18 September 322: Munychia 'was thus taken on 18 September 322 BC'. Athens gave up its navy, took a Macedonian garrison, lost 'possessions outside Attica' (Oropus, Samos) and its democracy ('the citizen body fell from 21,000 to 9,000'). [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: counterpart macedonian-empire to greek-city-states: the members return to the Greek city-states row (its /ledger/47, September 322), which Macedon then takes as vassals (macedonian-empire /ledger/30).]

September 322: the alliance is over with Athens's surrender; Hypereides was killed on 6 October and Demosthenes a week later. Only Aetolia fought on, under its own colour (aetolian-league). Cliopatria's shape runs to 319; it should end in 322.

wars.name: Lamian War

zones.text: the naval battles of Amorgos and the Echinades, 322

wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory': Thessaly recovered, Athens garrisoned and disfranchised, the Greek allies made separate terms; only the Aetolians held out.
wars.note: Boeotia, Euboea and the Acarnanians fought on the Macedonian side (infobox), hence greek-city-states on both sides of the blend.

certainty.note: An alliance of states drawn as one hatch: member lists are firm, their tribal boundaries approximate, and the Peloponnesian members joined over the winter.

sources.title: Lamian War
sources.note: Infobox 323-322, members, treaties of 27 October and 23 December 323, Crannon 6 August 322, Munychia 18 September 322, terms.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Athenian Coalition' row carries two unrelated shapes: 323-319 (Attica, Thessaly, Aetolia; this dossier) and 264-257 (Attica and Laconia), which is the Chremonidean War alliance of 267-261 and is reviewed in the new dossier chremonidean-alliance (split, reported in new_slugs). Cliopatria's Wikipedia title for the row, 'Peloponnesian War', and Wikidata Q33745 are wrong for both; the id is kept only because the schema asks for one, and the reviewer should replace it. Typed rebel so the compiler can hatch the revolt over the Macedonian vassal tint of 323-322 (rule 5); the Aetolians, a sovereign league, keep their own colour and appear only in the contest. Corrections: end in September 322 (not 319); membership widened to the page's list, with Boeotia and Euboea removed. Rhodes 'may not have formally joined' and is left out. [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: the admin-1 unit Dytiki Ellada (all of Western Greece, with Achaea and Acarnania) was replaced by Aetolia proper as Cliopatria's Aetolian League shape of 284: the Lamian War page lists the Aetolian League as a member but says 'Acarnania backed Macedonia (except Alyzeia)' and does not list Peloponnesian Achaea; Elis stays in through the Pirgos radius.]
